_readme: ATS boards discovered from public URL indexes (N3). One entry per board: vendor matches ATSAdapter.vendor, slug is company.ats_slug (Workday: '<host>/<site>'), name is null until a source names the company, first_seen and last_verified are ISO dates (last_verified null = never fetched), source is one or more of commoncrawl/wayback/hackernews joined with '+' (counts.by_source counts a board once per source that evidenced it, so it sums above the total). Build a board URL with dreamjob.adapters.ats.detect.board_url(vendor, slug) and find the adapter with detect.adapter_key_for(vendor). Liveness decays: re-verify every 30 days in the nightly job, never per campaign. Regenerate with scripts/import_board_registry.py.

composition: Seed shipped with the repository so a fresh install has targets before the importer is ever run (N3).

EU-weighted on the measured job-location shares of section 2.3: Recruitee (83% EU, 37% Benelux) and Personio (55% EU) are taken whole from the Common Crawl URL index, as are Teamtailor and Lever; Greenhouse (8% EU) and Ashby (18% EU) contribute only their HN 'Who is hiring' boards, which are current and self-selected, because taking them whole would triple the file for boards a Benelux campaign discards.

Excluded on purpose: Workday, because the URL indexes name only the tenant host while the adapter's slug is '<host>/<site>' and a guessed site name is a 404 that gets stored and re-probed (section 6.7); SmartRecruiters, because api.smartrecruiters.com allows LinkedInBot only, so the adapter is disabled (C6, IR-101); Wayback-only slugs, which are 27.5% live against 87.5% for a 2026 crawl and therefore belong to an operator's refresh rather than to a file every install ships.
last_verified is null on every row: no board here has been fetched by this installation. Liveness is the nightly job's to write, one request per slug, re-checked every 30 days (C8).

Boards resolved from named employers' own careers pages by scripts/resolve_employer_seed.py. The URL indexes above do not name the large employers a Benelux search is judged on - they run Workday or their own careers site - so those rows can only come from reading the employer's page. No slug is guessed; last_verified stays null because no other installation has fetched them.
provenance.notes: Operator-run monthly import, never a campaign step. index.commoncrawl.org and data.commoncrawl.org are robots-disallowed and are read here, outside the egress layer, as an open dataset under Common Crawl's terms of use; every other host is robots-checked. Liveness is not verified here: last_verified is written by the nightly job, one request per slug.
